# #202 Lapsing-first roster order
## Parent
#201
## What to build
A coach's roster ranks lapsing players first. Roster rows carry the number of new *lapsing* alerts (missed expected days, follow-up due). The roster urgency order's first key becomes that count. It is followed by the other new coach alerts plus pending program requests, then the existing keys unchanged. The order stays a strict, weightless tuple, and the roster still reads only catalog data.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Roster rows expose `alerts_new_lapsing`, counting only new (not acknowledged, not resolved) missed-day and follow-up-due alerts, read from catalog tables only. - [ ] The order ranks by new lapsing alerts, then other new alerts plus pending program requests, then missed-day streak, overdue follow-up, oldest last workout, and username, as in CONTEXT.md "Roster urgency order". - [ ] A player with one new missed-day alert ranks above a player with two new regression alerts (roster API test). - [ ] Acknowledged lapsing alerts do not count. - [ ] Pure ordering tests cover the lapsing/other split. Existing roster order tests still pass or are updated only where the new first key changes the expected order. - [ ] Listing the roster opens no player ledger.
